result.topic_en: Euler states his intention to derive true general principles for the equilibrium and motion of perfectly flexible and elastic threads, poses the general problem of finding the state of tension or bending at each element of a thread in equilibrium under arbitrary forces, and begins the solution by considering a thread AMB fixed at A and B.
result.transcription:
382 DE STATV AEQVILIBRII ET MOTV
fila simplicia siue perfecte flexibilia siue elastica, vti qui-
dem adhuc a Geometris sunt tractata accuratius sum con-
templaturus. Quum enim pleraeque solutiones, quae pas-
sim super hoc argumento reperiuntur, vel ex principiis
tantum particularibus vel saltem non satis clarit[?] et per-
spicuis sint deductae, operam dabo vt vera et generalia
principia, quibus determinatio figurae huiusmodi corporum
innititur ita dilucide exponam, vt non solum status ae-
quilibrii, sed etiam motus huiusmodi corporum inde inues-
tigari queat.
Problema generale.
Si filum siue perfecte flexile siue elasticum et in singulis punctis a viribus quibuscunque sollicitatum ad sta-
tum aequilibrii fuerit perductum; pro singulis eius ele-
mentis statum siue tensionis, siue inflexionis inuestigare.
Solutio.
Tab. VII. Fig. 3. I. Referat hic curua AMB huiusmodi filum a viribus
quibuscunque sollicitatum, quod in aequilibrio reperiatur
atque fixum sit in terminis A et B, atque manifestum est
in singulis huius fili punctis M dari certum tensionis siue
inflexionis statum, quem inde intelligere licet, quod si hoc
filum alicubi in M resecetur, vtraque portio AM et BM
extemplo longe aliam figuram sit acceptura, vnde neces-
sario sequitur in hoc puncto M, quamdiu ambae partes

items.english: I shall endeavour to set out so clearly the true and general principles on which the determination of the figure of such bodies rests, that not only the state of equilibrium but also the motion of such bodies can be investigated from them.

items.quote:
Si filum siue perfecte flexile siue elasticum et in singulis punctis a viribus quibuscunque sollicitatum ad sta-
tum aequilibrii fuerit perductum; pro singulis eius ele-
mentis statum siue tensionis, siue inflexionis inuestigare.
items.english: If a thread, either perfectly flexible or elastic, acted on at every point by arbitrary forces, has been brought to a state of equilibrium, to investigate for each of its elements the state either of tension or of bending.

items.quote:

in singulis huius fili punctis M dari certum tensionis siue

filum alicubi in M resecetur, vtraque portio AM et BM

items.english: It is evident that at every point M of this thread there is a definite state of tension or bending, which can be understood from the fact that if the thread is cut somewhere at M, each portion AM and BM would immediately take on a quite different figure.
